checks.finding: AC-008 (requirements.md:186) and AC-010 (requirements.md:188) both key their oracle to an undefined 'representative' sdd-forge component / plugin change, while OQ-006's resolution (requirements.md:368-370) fixes a Lite-vs-full track split ('the lite track is admissible for docs-only changes; everything else takes the full track'). Neither requirements.md nor acceptance-tests.md (TEST-008, TEST-010) states which component or change qualifies as representative, or that it must exercise the full track. Two implementers could each pick a different 'representative' change -- one docs-only (Lite track) and one plugin-code (full track) -- producing materially different fixtures; the docs-only choice would never exercise the developer-tooling/cli-library Pack's predicate/facet/gate machinery that REQ-006's advisory dogfood evidence exists to validate. This is a testability/observability gap in the Phase-1 acceptance criteria themselves, not an implementation detail, so it belongs to spec review. Major per calibration's 'missing observable acceptance criterion ... high-risk claim with no planned validation surface' bucket: it does not conflict with another requirement (not Critical) and it materially changes what gets validated (not Minor).

REQ-004 (requirements.md:62-68) requires the component inventory to preserve a distinguishable, non-blanket credential/write characteristic for 'credential-bearing CI MCP' specifically versus the read-only local MCP services; AC-007 (requirements.md:185) makes this an oracle: 'Characteristic tests distinguish plugin/MCP/installer/CI/release boundaries, including the CI-MCP credential and release-write cases.' But OQ-001's resolved decomposition (requirements.md:274-284) merges every MCP service into one single `mcp` component ('the MCP service group under mcp/'), and OQ-002's resolved ownership map (requirements.md:295-306) places release automation and metadata (`.github/**`, CHANGELOG.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, package.json) into the cross-cutting/shared classification rather than any owned component. Per the schema surface this package itself relies on (investigation.md:41, INV-005: 'Component records can carry ... seven boolean characteristics'), only owned components carry characteristic fields; a single merged `mcp` component can hold only one set of those booleans, not a distinct one for the credential-bearing ci-mcp sub-service noted separately at investigation.md:47 (INV-011: 'ci-mcp alone consumes a read-only GitHub token' among three otherwise read-only MCP servers). An implementer building AC-007 has no component in the human-approved OQ-001/OQ-002 model that can hold a distinct CI-MCP or release-write characteristic without either violating the fixed eight-component decomposition or inventing an undocumented sub-component/override mechanism. This is a direct requirement-level conflict discoverable purely inside requirements.md, not an implementation detail, so it belongs to spec review. Critical because it makes AC-007 impossible to satisfy under the human-approved, 'implement as-is' OQ-001/OQ-002 resolutions without a new human ruling -- an impossible acceptance criterion under the fixed decomposition.

requirements.md's Edge Cases section (line 244) states: 'Approver registry changes between rollback request and effective time: re-run approval validation with the current registry,' and OQ-004's resolution (requirements.md:335-339) makes this a named mechanism: 'A registry-membership change is itself a recorded registry update and re-evaluates the branch.' None of the REQ-009 acceptance rows -- AC-016/TEST-016 (multi-identity), AC-017/TEST-017 (solo timing), AC-018/TEST-018 (unsigned/self-approved/duplicate/unbound) -- test a registry-cardinality change occurring between rollback request and effective time (e.g., a second identity being registered during a solo-branch's 24-hour cooldown, forcing a branch re-evaluation to two-party). A task author decomposing REQ-009 into tests has no acceptance row instructing them to build this fixture, and an implementer could ship rollback logic that reads the approver registry once at request time rather than re-validating at effective time, silently violating the named edge case. This is an acceptance-tests.md coverage gap for a requirements.md-named edge case in a governance/security boundary (rollback), squarely spec review's scope. Major per calibration: not Critical because the base rollback boundary is otherwise tested; not Minor because it is a named governance edge case, not a mere clarification.

The Assumptions section (requirements.md:257-265) lists four assumptions; each is either resolved (issue #197/#187 bodies reconciled, per investigation.md's Issue-Reconciliation Result, lines 81-87) or explicitly flagged as a decision/verification step required before further work rather than silently assumed -- e.g., 'A1-A8 availability is mutable shared state and must be re-verified at spec review and implementation, never assumed from this draft' (requirements.md:261-262), which investigation.md INV-018 (line 54) independently substantiates by showing A5 exists only on a feature branch outside this branch's Active Spec list. No assumption in this section is left silently unresolved.

REQ-001 (requirements.md:37-44) requires the protected approval publication workflow and forbids an unsigned or agent-approved sidecar, tested by AC-002 (requirements.md:180: 'Publication tests reject missing/invalid approval binding and demonstrate the human-copy boundary'). REQ-009 (requirements.md:108-116) and OQ-004's resolution (requirements.md:335-346) fix a mechanically-selected two-party/solo-plus-cooldown rollback boundary reusing signed Ed25519 evidence, tested by AC-016/017/018 (requirements.md:194-196). These approval/governance boundaries are testable as stated; the check is in scope (not SKIP) because REQ-001, REQ-008, and REQ-009 all imply a human-approval or irreversible-change boundary.

Because OQ-001's fixed, human-approved eight-component decomposition (requirements.md:274-284) cannot represent the distinct CI-MCP credential characteristic REQ-004/AC-007 requires (requirements.md:62-68, 185; see the CONTRADICTION finding above), a design reviewer inheriting this package would have to invent -- without a human ruling -- either a new sub-component boundary inside the fixed 'eight components' resolution or an undocumented characteristic-override mechanism for cross-cutting paths. Choosing between those is a product/architecture decision that belongs to spec review's OQ process (OQ-001 was already run for exactly this purpose), not to implementation-policy review. This is a downstream-readiness gap distinct from the contradiction itself: even if a reviewer worked around the conflict, they would be inventing missing product behavior this gate exists to catch before handoff. Major per calibration's 'missing constraint' framing; not Critical because the readiness gap is a consequence of, not identical to, the underlying contradiction already reported at Critical severity.

No `domain/` directory exists at the project root (confirmed by the permitted domain/-existence check and corroborated by investigation.md's own note: 'Domain-Sync: domain-sync skipped: no domain/ directory', investigation.md:31), so the DOMAIN-CONFORMANCE scoped surface is absent and the check is recorded as skipped per its explicit skip condition.
